rulings.reason: The description already gives basis beyond [0190] for claims 44 and 67. [0311] (statement 1.14) claims 'a flow path through a wall of the seat ring' with no location; [0191] says that with the wall slots 'the outer surface of the seat ring 30 can be retained along its whole length', so the slots are expressly not tied to the free portion 37; and [0171] describes strut-pattern cells 'closed at rest' that provide 'a route for the purge flow when the wall deforms'. The claims' 'closed at rest and open on the radial expansion' covers both closing means of [0190] ('lie against the bore' or 'their edges abut'), which is a generalisation of two stated alternatives, not an intermediate one.

[0067] defines 'closed at rest' as the surfaces being 'in the position that those surfaces take when no load is applied ... by the load-applying surface' and says it 'does not require closure that is gas-tight to a stated degree'. On that definition any unloaded clearance is 'closed', so the limitation in claims 1, 2 and 67 separates nothing from a permanent bypass that widens under load. The drawing instruction for FIG. 4A (registry.md) draws the free portion 37 'with a small radial clearance already shown' to the core body bore, which contradicts [0124] ('In FIG. 1 the purge gap 60 is closed and is drawn as a single line') and [0187] ('closes the purge gap 60 at rest by line contact'). The best defence, that [0065] and [0124] say the gap is closed at rest, fails because [0067] is the definition that governs those words. Both reviewers found it. A positive test of closure needs the inventor's confirmation.

[0007] attributes an enlarged bore, a fluoropolymer-coated sealing face, a rigid seat and a removable insert to 'US2019/0123456A1'. The matter's prior-art index (runs/r1/prior-art/INDEX.md, row S1) records that document as 'FICTIONAL US 2019/0123456 A1 ... not a real publication and was not searched for or fetched'. [0013] ('In the documents referred to above') draws it into the statement of the problem. No passage of the package can defend a citation to a document that does not exist as described: it is an inaccurate acknowledgement at the EPO (Rule 42(1)(b)), an admission and a disclosure-statement problem in the US, and an easy point for a UK opponent. Deleting [0007] and adjusting [0013] narrows nothing.
Duplicate of F-32-1 (same reviewer, same objection to claim 3 as a seat ring limited only by intended use, same least-narrowing action). Ruled there.

[0058] defines 'seat ring' as a tubular element 'retained in the core body' whose wall converts 'an axial load applied by the purge shoulder'. [0050] applies the definitions 'in the claims', and [0063] defines 'purge shoulder' as 'a surface of the poppet'. Claim 20 through claim 15 recites a seat ring loaded by 'a collar that is a separate part carried by the poppet' ([0153]); [0155] loads the seat ring through a spring seat washer, 'not the poppet 40'; claim 3 and [0162] claim a seat ring 'supplied separately', not yet retained. The drafter's best defence, the proviso 'unless the context requires otherwise' in [0050], is a weak answer to an express definition, and the EPO will raise Art. 84 on the inconsistency. Corrected to medium: the cure is a description amendment to [0058] (and the matching locked-terminology row) with no claim change, and no claim falls meanwhile.

Duplicate of F-32-5: the same inventive-step objection that the inspection at [0287] and the concession at [0140]/[0289] do not show the effect the application attributes to the purge gap, and the same combination (US4044791A or US5918628A with US5924444A). The two reviewers found it independently; it is ruled on F-32-5.

Duplicate of F-32-5, which makes the same problem-and-solution attack on [0010]/[0013] against [0287], [0289] and the unidentified comparison cores of [0282], with the same fallback proposal (an independent claim to the tested combination). Ruled there.

figures.md states for FIGS. 11 and 12 'candidate alternative constructions identified during design-around analysis; not built, not tested, and not stated in the inventor's disclosure ... pending inventor confirmation', and for FIG. 13A the same; FIG. 4 is described as giving 'a concrete, drawable resolution' of the fit band and free portion. The registry prescribes captions such as 'Candidate alternative seat-ring geometries; not built or tested'. Claims 40 to 43 (FIG. 11), 44 and 67 (wall slots 204, FIG. 12B) and 26 and 66 (fit band 35, free portion 37, relief 202, FIGS. 4 and 12A) claim that matter, and [0176]-[0178], [0186]-[0190] present it as 'In some embodiments' with nothing to show it is unconfirmed. No paragraph answers the provenance: the package itself records it as unconfirmed. Whatever the inventor answers at the gate, the text must change (confirmed matter kept without captions; unconfirmed matter deleted or its contributor recorded).

Duplicate of F-32-6, which makes the same enablement attack (direction of opening, load path at [0113] against the FIG. 2 instruction, [0134] against [0172] and claim 24 against claim 22, the missing inlet, and [0202]) in fuller form. Ruled there.
Duplicate of F-32-4: the same arithmetic inconsistency in Example 1 (forty 24-hour holds recorded between 12 and 20 August 2026, [0283]). Both reviewers found it; it is ruled on F-32-4.

The premise that the fit band and free portion are disclosed only with the core body bore relief is answered by the text. [0229] states that 'the retention by axial clamping or by staking is combined with the free portion 37', which is the free portion without the interference-fit/relief pairing, and claim 66 as filed is itself basis for a seat ring with a fit band 35 and a free portion 37 and no relief (the relief is a core body feature, recited only in claim 26). The [0014]/claim 1 difference is deliberate genus drafting: [0014] states 'radial deflection' and claim 1 the narrower 'radial expansion'; a Summary broader than claim 1 is basis for amendment, not an inconsistency that needs correcting at filing.

Claim 19 recites a purge gap width of 0.10 mm to 0.25 mm; [0097] defines it only as 'the radial size of the purge gap when the purge gap is fully open' and [0237]/[0280] give no method of measuring it in an assembled valve core. Claims 11, 12 and 53 recite crack pressures and over-travel differentials with no stated test condition, and [0274] records that 'the rate at which the floor pump delivered air was not recorded', while [0288] confirms over-travel only 'by an audible snap'. [0230] says the ranges are what 'the inventors consider' and 'have not been explored by test'; [0290] gives 'no value ... for the purge gap width' in PEEK (claims 30, 31, 74, 75). The drafter's best defence, that austenite finish temperature and crack pressure are measured by conventional methods, answers claim 29 but not the purge gap width or the over-travel differential. Medium is right: dependent claims only, in a predictable mechanical art.

Duplicate in substance. The US multiple-dependency and fee points are ruled on F-30-23 (both reviewers). The objection to claim 50 (a product limited by a tyre chamber containing sealant) is ruled on F-30-13, with the same fix at [0327]. The remaining points do not amount to a defect: Rule 43(1) EPC requires the two-part form only 'wherever appropriate', and claim 38 recites what happens when the purge gap of the claimed valve core is open, which is supported at [0016] and [0194].

Claim 49 ('the core body being formed in the valve stem') depends on claim 47, which requires the valve core to be 'received in a bore of the valve stem'; [0159] confirms the integral core 'is not threaded into it', so the two cannot both be met. Claim 50, a tyre valve, is limited by 'the tyre chamber contains sealant', an entity outside the claimed product; [0327] (statement 2.5) already frames this correctly as 'A tyre chamber fitted with the tyre valve'. Claim 45 bounds the purge gap of a valve core by 'a bore of a valve stem (10) in which the valve core is fitted', which the valve core claim does not contain; [0189] supports moving it under claim 47. No passage answers these; the fixes are in-place and narrow nothing.

Duplicate of F-30-1: the same definiteness objection to the definition of 'closed at rest' in [0067] and the FIG. 4A clearance, with the same fix (a positive closure test in [0067], confirmed by the inventor). Ruled there.

Confirmed on the text. No figure shows the collar of claim 15 ([0153]), the spring constructions of claims 9 and 10 ([0144]-[0146]; figures.md says FIG. 5 is 'deliberately drawn without specifying how the two-rate characteristic is physically produced') or the valve stem bore of claim 45 ([0189]). FIG. 13A has no brief description: [0049] describes only FIG. 13B. Numerals 220, 402 and 404 are in registry.md but appear nowhere in the description as reference signs. The registry prescribes text captions on the drawings ('Candidate alternative seat-ring geometries; not built or tested ...') for FIGS. 11, 12 and 13A. 37 CFR 1.83(a) and 1.84(p)(5), Rule 46(2) EPC. Formal and curable; medium stands.

The one point not already in F-30-15 is confirmed: claim 1 recites 'a purge gap (60, 146)' and registry.md registers 146 as 'purge gap' in FIG. 9, but 146 never appears as a reference sign in the description ([0181]-[0182] describe FIG. 9 without it). The FIG. 13A, numeral 220 and caption points duplicate F-30-15. Corrected to low: a missing reference sign is a formal matter with no effect on scope.

The US 112(f) half duplicates F-30-18, which is ruled there. The EPO essential-features half fails on its premise that a free portion is needed for the result. Claim 1 does not recite a pressed-in ring, and the description opens a purge gap without a free portion in several forms: wall slots with the outer surface 'retained along its whole length' ([0191]), the wiper ring 144 of the two-piece seat, where 'the seal at rest is made on the rigid seat 140' ([0181]-[0182]), and the slotted sleeve 170 ([0176]). A feature that the description shows is replaceable is not essential under Art. 84.

'Radially deflectable element' uses 'element', a nonce word, qualified only by what it does ([0099]: 'deflected radially by the axial load ... that thereby opens the purge gap'). [0106] states that each functional term 'covers each structure described herein that performs the function', which echoes the corresponding-structure wording of 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and invites a court to confine the terms to the described structures and their equivalents. The best defence, that 'surface' and 'geometry' name structure, answers 'load-applying surface' in part but not 'element' or 'return bias' ([0101]: 'an element, or a combination of elements'). US-only exposure; medium stands. Counsel may accept the 112(f) reading, given the number of described structures.

Accurate as a statement of law but no defect in the text. The finding itself proposes no change to claim 2. The supplier's product is reached directly by claims 1, 47 and 77 (valve core, tyre valve, valve core with the seat ring), and a spring whose over-travel differential ordinary pumping rarely reaches still infringes claim 1, which recites the structure and not a threshold pressure. The indirect-infringement limits described are inherent to any method-of-use claim. The kit-with-instructions suggestion, with basis at [0276], is an option for counsel, not a deficiency.

Claim 77 is a valve core defined through the seat ring of claim 3 and is not within claim 1: it omits, for example, the requirement that the load-applying surface be 'spaced from the radially deflectable element throughout the normal stroke'. That makes two independent valve-core claims, a credible Rule 43(2) EPC objection, and none of the exceptions obviously fits two valve cores. Unity a posteriori depends on F-32-1: if claim 3 is held to be limited only by intended use and falls, claims 1-2 and 3-4 share no special technical feature. US restriction among claims 1, 2, 3 and 4 is to be expected. The cure (recast claim 77 as dependent, or delete it) narrows nothing in claim 1.

[0210] ('A spring-tempered metal is not proposed for a continuous convoluted wall 34') is guidance that steers the skilled person to the suitable materials; it does not show that claims 20-26 cannot be carried out. The description names the materials that work for the convoluted wall (superelastic NiTi, [0184], [0279]; polymer, [0208]), and a claim that also covers materials the description itself advises against is not insufficient where the working ones are identified. The PEEK point ([0290]) duplicates F-30-11, where it is ruled. No verifiable fact is offered that raises a serious doubt beyond what F-30-11 already records.

Upheld on one point not raised elsewhere: [0065] defines the purge gap as 'opened in the over-travel by the deflection that the load-applying surface produces', while [0216] has the thermal variant open 'the purge gap 60 without a pump', with the poppet seated (FIG. 10). The same term is used against its own definition. The unity and US restriction points duplicate F-30-20. The unclaimed embodiments ([0179], statement 7.1 at [0347]) and the numbered statements at [0297]-[0348] are grant-stage adaptations at the EPO, not filing defects, and the finding itself advises keeping the statements as basis for amendment. Corrected to low: the definitional conflict is cured by wording [0065] as 'in the first aspect'.

Verified on claims.md: 45 of the 86 claims are multiple dependent, and at least 35 depend on another multiple dependent claim; for example, claim 13 ('any one of claims 1 and 5 to 12') includes claim 11 ('any one of claims 5 to 10'), and claim 86 ('any one of claims 62 to 69') includes claims 65, 67 and 68. 37 CFR 1.75(c) makes those claims improper in the US; they will be objected to and not examined, and every proper multiple dependent claim attracts the surcharge. The EPO (Rule 45) and UK excess-claims fees apply to an 86-claim set. Both reviewers found it. Medium stands: a US claim set with single dependencies cures it without narrowing.

Claim 85 recites 'about 0.03 mm on diameter' and claim 73 'a nominal composition of 55.8 wt% nickel'. [0056] defines 'about' only as 'the ordinary manufacturing tolerance and measurement tolerance for the parameter concerned', with no figure, and [0250]/[0259] give none. An EPO clarity objection is likely for the European set. Low stands: dependent claims only, and deleting the qualifiers is a narrow cure.

No error in the text is identified; the finding describes a choice between EPO and US drafting practice that counsel makes per jurisdiction. The EPO expects the problem to be stated (Rule 42(1)(c)) and [0010]-[0013] do so. The US narrowing effect of [0015] is raised, with its claim consequence, in F-32-3; the test dates at [0283] fall to be corrected under F-32-4; the inaccurate acknowledgement of [0007] is ruled on F-30-2. 'Presta-pattern' is used as a trade designation, with the stem dimensions given at [0157] ('an outer diameter of 6 mm').

The text supplies the frame of reference. [0117] states that the purge shoulder 44 'is located below the sealing face 42, that is, it is spaced from the sealing face 42 along the valve axis', and [0063] uses 'below the sealing face' in the same sense; claim 14 is read in the light of that gloss. [0112] identifies the 'upper edge' as the end edge that 'forms a sealing edge 32', which fixes it without reference to the drawing orientation.

Claim 3 claims a seat ring that is tubular, has 'a sealing edge ... at one end ... for seating a sealing face ... of a poppet', and 'a wall having a load-converting geometry'. The poppet, the load-applying surface, the normal stroke, the over-travel, the main passage and the purge gap belong to a valve core the claim does not contain, and limit the ring only to what is suitable for that use. The drafter's best defence, that the ring must actually expand radially under an axial load and recover, is a real structural capability, and no saved reference discloses it: US11549591B1 FIG. 10 has a 'cylindrical sidewall 814' with a downstream flange that 'may be planar, undulating, or curved' to seal, and says nothing of axial load producing radial expansion; EP3171056A1 moves its wave-shaped ring radially on heating, not under axial load. So novelty is arguable, but the defence does not meet the inventive-step and clarity objections: [0171] equates the load-converting geometry with a 'zig-zag pattern or a pattern of diamond-shaped cells' cut in tube, [0166] acknowledges an undulating resilient metal seat for a poppet, and a ring defined by reference to parts it does not include draws an Art. 84 objection. A credible rejection that needs an amendment; high stands. The scope trade-off (for example reciting the fit band and free portion of claim 66, or the bore-bounded gap of claim 65 proposed in F-32-2) is for the human.

Duplicate of F-32-1 (claim 3 distinguished from the art only by intended use), ruled there, where its alternative amendment (claim 65 and [0167] features) is noted. Its evidence is also overstated: in US11549591B1 FIG. 10 the sidewall 814 is 'cylindrical' and only the downstream flanged portion 820 'may be ... undulating', and nothing in that reference or in EP3171056A1 (radial movement on heating above the transformation temperature) converts an axial load into radial expansion.

The reading is correct on the text: claims 1 and 2 require the load-applying surface to be 'spaced from the radially deflectable element throughout the normal stroke' and the purge gap 'closed ... throughout the normal stroke', [0071] defines the normal stroke by that spacing, and [0015] calls the two travel ranges features that 'act together'. A construction in which the surface rests on the element from closure falls outside every independent claim. Whether anything can be done turns on facts outside the package: (a) whether the inventor conceived a contact-from-the-start form (the description has none), and (b) whether a claim without the spacing limitation would survive US4044791A, whose floating valve seat is 'yieldably biased into engagement with a poppet' ([0008]), which suggests the limitation may be what distinguishes that art. Resolved by the inventor's answer at the embodiment gate and counsel's view of US4044791A. Corrected to medium: it is a residual design-around risk, not a rejection.

[0283] defines one inflation cycle as inflating, 'holding for a period of 24 hours', and deflating, and records the test 'as carried out from 12 August to 20 August of 2026', nine days. [0285]/[0286] report prototypes completing 40 cycles and conventional cores failing at 12, 14 and 18, with leak-down stated 'in a period of 24 hours'. Forty 24-hour holds cannot fit in nine days, and no passage explains a shorter hold. Example 1 is the only data ([0278] calls it 'an actual example'), and [0003] and [0012] rely on it. Both reviewers found it. Only the laboratory record can say which figure is wrong; nothing may be adjusted without it. High stands: in the US it is a candour matter for counsel before filing.

[0013] attributes the purge gap's effect to directing air 'across a surface of the valve core on which sealant film accumulates', and [0136] says the air purge 'acts on sealant film present on those surfaces'. The application's own inspection finds the opposite on those surfaces: 'Cured sealant film was present on the outer surface of the seat ring 30 in the region of the purge gap 60' ([0287], repeated at [0140]). The surfaces found clean, the sealing edge 32 and the sealing face 42, bound the main passage. [0289] concedes that 'the test does not show the separate contribution of each cleaning action', and [0282] identifies the comparison cores only as 'standard Presta-pattern valve cores of a single manufacturer'. The drafter's best defence, the last sentence of [0287] that the sealing surfaces stayed clean, supports an effect of over-travel plus shape recovery, not of the purge gap. The combination offered (staged opening, [0008], US4044791A/US5918628A, with the outward-deforming, self-returning ring of US5924444A, [0009]) is credible against claims 1, 2, 3, 38 and 57. Both reviewers found it (see F-30-5, F-30-6). High stands.

Each gap is on the face of the text. (1) [0124] puts the purge gap between the outer surface of the seat ring and the surrounding bore, and [0081] defines radial expansion as 'an outward movement', which moves that surface towards the bore; no passage says what contact closes the gap at rest in the tested construction or why outward movement breaks it. [0187] gives 'line contact at one end of the core body bore relief' only for the relief embodiment, which [0202] says was not the tested construction. (2) [0113] applies the load 'for example at its upper edge', which [0112] makes the sealing edge; the FIG. 2 instruction in registry.md puts the purge shoulder 'at the fit-band end', which [0186] places 'next to the locating shoulder'. (3) [0134] and [0170] ('the waves flatten') and claim 22 have the convolution flatten; [0172] says the single outward bow 'increases under axial load', and claim 24 claims that bow in dependence on claim 22. (4) Only the exit is described ([0194]); no inlet to the gap is identified. (5) [0112] says the tested ring was 'pressed into the core body with a light interference fit', and [0202] excludes the fit band, free portion and relief from the tested construction. The best defence, that a convoluted ring expanding into a clearance is intuitive, does not answer the contradictions, which are the verifiable facts an opponent needs. Both reviewers found it (F-30-8). High stands; it needs the inventor's account of the prototype.

[0179] describes a working alternative: a conical disc spring whose rim 'seals on a face at rest', flattened by the load-applying surface in over-travel so that 'a purge gap opens at the face', and then states that 'its deflection is not a radial expansion'. [0180] adds that the deformation may be 'radial, axial, tilting or a combination'. Every independent claim requires 'a radial expansion of the radially deflectable element' (claims 1, 2) or 'of the wall' (claim 3). No passage brings [0179] back within the claims, and the applicant's own sentence works against an equivalents argument; in the US, subject matter disclosed and not claimed is exposed to dedication. High stands because the fix requires a new or broadened independent claim and cannot be made after filing. The provenance of [0179] is not recorded in the package ('No figure shows this form'), so it should be confirmed with the inventor together with F-30-7 before it is claimed.
Duplicate of F-30-2: the same fictional citation of US2019/0123456A1 at [0007] and its reach through [0013], with the same fix (delete [0007]). Both reviewers found it; it is ruled on F-30-2.
